transcript.text:
*looks up from organizing spools of thread behind the counter*

Good afternoon, sir! Welcome to Whitmore & Sons Fine Tailoring. I'm afraid Mr. Whitmore has departed for New York on business and won't return for several weeks yet. 

*notices the tall figure and the package under his arm*

Is there something I might help you with today? Perhaps you're here to place an order, or...

*eyes the wrapped garment with a hint of concern*

...is that one of our pieces?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Ah, good afternoon to you as well. Yes, I am indeed here regarding the garment you see before you. I must say, I am rather disappointed with the quality of the suit that was delivered to me. The stitching is uneven, one sleeve is noticeably shorter than the other, and the fabric seems to be of a lesser quality than what was promised. I had high expectations for Whitmore & Sons Fine Tailoring, and it pains me to see such a lack of attention to detail in the workmanship.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*straightens up, clasping hands together with a polite but firm expression*

I see. Well, sir, I do apologize that you're dissatisfied, but I must ask—when did you collect this garment? And you did sign the receipt upon pickup, did you not?

*moves toward the counter, pulling out a large ledger book*

You see, all our custom orders are considered final once they leave the premises. Mr. Whitmore is most particular about this policy. The receipt clearly states that no alterations or refunds are given once the garment has been accepted and taken from the shop.

*looks up with a somewhat sympathetic but unyielding gaze*

Now, if there had been an issue at the time of collection, that would have been the moment to raise it. But if you've already taken possession and signed for it...

*trails off, shaking head slightly*

I'm afraid my hands are quite tied in the matter, sir. Even were I inclined to help—which I assure you I would be under different circumstances—I haven't the authority to override shop policy, especially with Mr. Whitmore away for weeks yet.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
I appreciate your adherence to the shop's policies, and I understand the predicament in which this places us. However, the discrepancies in this suit were not readily apparent until I had the opportunity to examine it more closely outside the confines of this establishment. The issues with the stitching and the fabric quality only became evident upon further inspection.

While I recognize the challenges presented by Mr. Whitmore's absence, I implore you to consider the reputation of Whitmore & Sons Fine Tailoring and the importance of upholding a standard of excellence in your craft. Surely, there must be a way for us to address these concerns and ensure that the workmanship aligns with the expectations set by your esteemed establishment.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*shifts weight uncomfortably, glancing between Mr. Lincoln and the ledger, then back again*

Sir, I... I do hear your concerns, and I don't doubt your sincerity in expressing them. Truly, I don't. 

*rubs the back of neck, clearly torn*

But you must understand my position. I'm merely the assistant here—I've been entrusted to mind the shop, take orders, collect payments, but Mr. Whitmore was most explicit before his departure. "No exceptions to the policy," he said. "I've seen too many customers claim dissatisfaction after wearing a garment to an event, only to seek a refund afterward."

*pauses, studying the tall man before him*

Now, I can see you're a gentleman of principle, and perhaps this truly is a matter of workmanship. But without Mr. Whitmore here to inspect the piece himself and make that determination... 

*spreads hands apologetically*

What would you have me do, sir? I cannot authorize a refund—I'd likely lose my position for it. I cannot promise alterations when I don't know the tailor's schedule upon his return. The policy stands as written on your receipt, and I simply haven't the authority to contravene it.

*softens slightly*

Might I at least take your name and particulars? I could ensure Mr. Whitmore contacts you immediately upon his return in three weeks' time?

Please do take down my name and contact information. I shall leave it in your care, trusting that you will convey my concerns to Mr. Whitmore upon his return. I am Abraham Lincoln, and I can be reached at the law office of Lincoln & Herndon in Springfield. I shall await Mr. Whitmore's communication in due course.

Thank you for your attention to this matter, and I appreciate your willingness to assist within the confines of the shop's policies.
